correctness.rationale: For a mixed word, each starting position belongs to one maximal circular run of symbol a and is specified there by its remaining length t. Every row followed by a letter smaller than a sorts before every row followed by a larger letter; t increases in the former class and decreases in the latter. At equal t the post-run continuation determines order, preserved by letter-dependent dilation since the shared prefix is expanded identically. Identical periodic tails determine the backward circular letters too, hence ties cannot affect the output. At t=q h_a the preceding letters form the fixed word B(q); the h_a-1 intervening levels each contribute R(q) copies of a. This proves the entire last-column product, including for periodic words. For h_a>=2 every inserted factor is nonempty, so varying its length cannot change any run head, including across block boundaries. Monochromatic words are immediate, and direct rotation sorting gives BWT(011)=110 versus BWT(0011)=1010, showing sharpness even when just one exponent is 1. An independently written bounded reproduction passed 23,226 comparisons of full last columns and heads, all ternary words of length 1–7 with exponents 2 or 3 on present letters. The uploaded verifier was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: Proof is for the linear last column of the cyclic, sentinel-free BWT, with constant expansion factor per symbol. The independent reproduction covers only the stated finite test domain.

value.rationale: BWT run counts measure clustering; prior single-letter monotonicity leaves open whether further expansion still changes that clustering. The proof gives an exact, sharp universal cutoff and a stronger ordered invariant, while the full factorization specifies how run lengths can still change. This is useful for predicting cyclic BWT structure without sorting the expanded word.
residual_risks: No complexity improvement for a particular implementation, or extension to sentineled BWT, is established.
